author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic holds by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name. Reachable by its address alone; no pagination.
acceptance_criteria: The specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic holds by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name (first name then last name, e.g. Helen Leary)
A specialty held by no veterinarian is still listed, with no veterinarian shown under it
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster
All specialties render on one page, with no pagination
The page is served when its address is requested directly; no navigation entry and no inbound link to it is added
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, are presented in a stable, repeatable order
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged; this view is read-only)
A visible navigation entry or an inbound link to the specialty directory (deferred to a possible follow-up request)
notes: Inverse view of the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001). Open question: exact sort key for specialties and for veterinarians under each is unspecified; narrowest reading requires a deterministic order, exact key settled at implementation. Full name format is first name then last name per the request.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: New read-only route in the existing vet feature package, following the vet-directory read pattern (controller -> VetRepository -> Thymeleaf template, no service layer). GET /specialties.html inverts the vet->specialty association: it lists every Specialty (including those held by no Veterinarian) with the Veterinarians holding each. Recorded in docs/system-design.md#contracts (VetController, VetRepository, Specialty rows now cite REQ-VET-003). No new module, no new pattern, no ADR: the inversion is orchestration in the controller, matching the codebase's observed 'business logic in controllers' shape. Verified against source: VetController.showVetList / VetRepository.findAll(Pageable) / Vet.getSpecialties (grep on vet package; no IDE oracle connected, weaker basis).
integration_points: VetRepository gains List<Specialty> findSpecialties() via explicit @Query("SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name") + @Transactional(readOnly=true); an explicit @Query returns Specialty even though the repository is typed Repository<Vet,Integer>. Do NOT annotate it @Cacheable("vets") — that shared cache region holds vet lists; leave the new method uncached.

VetController gains @GetMapping("/specialties.html") returning view name vets/specialtyList; builds an ordered Map<Specialty,List<Vet>> (LinkedHashMap) from findSpecialties() (keys, in name order) plus findAll() (source of holders), and adds it as model attribute 'specialties'.
Template vets/specialtyList.html reuses the layout fragment with the 'vets' menu tab selected; NO new nav item and NO inbound link (deferred per NG note / acceptance bullet 5).

Reuse EXISTING message keys only: #{specialties} (heading), #{vets} (holders column), #{none} (empty specialty). Introducing any new key would force all 11 locale bundles to satisfy REQ-LANG-002 — avoid it.

patterns.description: read-only @GetMapping('/vets.html') that loads from VetRepository and returns a vets/* view name — the template to mirror for /specialties.html (minus pagination)
Vet.getSpecialties() already sorts specialties by name; reuse Comparator.comparing(NamedEntity::getName) as the specialty ordering key, matching this convention and the specialties_name DB index
existing pattern for rendering each specialty and the #{none} fallback; the specialty page inverts it — iterate specialties, render holders, show #{none} when the holder list is empty

risks.risk: Identity-equality trap: BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode (identity only). Specialty instances from findSpecialties() are different objects than those reachable via Vet.getSpecialties(), so matching a vet's specialty to a directory key by object equality will silently miss and drop holders.
risks.mitigation: Invert by specialty id: build Map<Integer,List<Vet>> keyed by Specialty.getId() from the vets, then assemble the ordered output by looking each name-ordered Specialty's id up in that map (getOrDefault empty list). Never use Specialty as a lookup key across the two queries.

risks.risk: A specialty held by no vet must still appear (acceptance bullet 2); iterating vets alone would omit it.
risks.mitigation: Drive the output from findSpecialties() (the full specialty list), not from the vets — every specialty is a row; the holder list is empty for unheld ones and renders #{none}.

risks.risk: Non-deterministic holder order under a specialty (acceptance edge case 1).
risks.mitigation: Sort each specialty's holders by last name then first name: Comparator.comparing(Vet::getLastName).thenComparing(Vet::getFirstName). Deterministic and repeatable; id is an acceptable alternative key.

risks.risk: VetControllerTests is a @WebMvcTest slice using @MockitoBean VetRepository (pre-existing, in tension with the repo-wide no-mock policy but the established shape of THIS file). The new findSpecialties() must be stubbed in setup or the specialty tests see an empty directory.
risks.mitigation: Add given(this.vets.findSpecialties()).willReturn(...) alongside the existing findAll() stubs; follow the existing file's slice-test style rather than re-deriving test policy in this slice.

notes: Verdict new (not minor): a new user-facing route/page plus an inversion mechanic absent elsewhere, worth recording in current-state memory (Contracts rows updated). No ADR — the reuse-VetRepository-vs-new-SpecialtyRepository and controller-inversion choices are low-stakes and reversible. Open question on ordering (prd Open Questions; prd-entry notes) is RESOLVED here: specialties ordered by stored name ascending via ORDER BY s.name (deterministic per vendor, matches PetTypeRepository/Vet.getSpecialties/the specialties_name index); holders ordered by last name then first name. file_targets keep the query on VetRepository per the prd-entry; a dedicated SpecialtyRepository is an equally valid, slightly more idiomatic alternative if the implementer prefers one-aggregate-per-repository, but it adds a file beyond the recorded target. Model attribute may instead be a small package-private view record if the Map<Specialty,List<Vet>> iteration reads awkward in Thymeleaf; the map keeps footprint minimal and matches the codebase's pass-a-collection idiom. No design-doc-autofix records present; autofix audit skipped.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Specialty name ordering is not asserted. PRD edge case 1 for REQ-VET-003 requires specialties presented in a stable order. The setup stub returns [radiology(), surgery()] which is already alphabetical, so a controller defect that ignored findSpecialties() order or reversed it would leave all five specialty tests green. No test contains an assertion of the form indexOf("radiology") < indexOf("surgery"). Holder ordering under a specialty is correctly tested in specialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians (Douglas < Leary); specialty-level ordering has no parallel assertion.

All five new test methods omit the leading 'the' required by the project BDD naming school (testing-principles.md § Test Naming: 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}'). Current names: specialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians, specialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName, specialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian, specialtyDirectoryShouldOmitAVeterinarianHoldingNoSpecialty, specialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage.
findings.fix: Prefix each method name with 'the': theSpecialtyDirectoryShould...

approved_aspects: Id-based inversion is well-exercised: setup intentionally returns fresh Specialty instances from findSpecialties() distinct from those held by vets, directly targeting the BaseEntity identity trap called out in the design-block
Holder ordering under a specialty is correctly asserted positionally (indexOf("Linda Douglas") < indexOf("Helen Leary")): covers PRD edge case 1 for holder sub-ordering
No-specialty vet exclusion (James Carter) and unheld-specialty appearance (surgery + none) each have dedicated tests mapped to the matching PRD acceptance criteria
No-pagination assertion checks absence of the ?page= query parameter in rendered content
Mockito @MockitoBean usage is tolerated per testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy for this pre-existing @WebMvcTest slice
Factory methods (james(), helen(), linda(), radiology(), surgery()) are used for all object construction, satisfying the factory-method rule for new test code
AssertJ assertThat() is used for the positional ordering assertion; MockMvc Hamcrest matchers are standard for this layer

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The comment wraps so that the word "one" sits alone on its own line ("// one"), severed from "unheld" above it. A future reader scanning the block will pause on "// one" as if it were a standalone thought. The sentence is "so an unheld one still becomes a row" — reflow it so "unheld one" stays on the same line, or reword to avoid the awkward split (e.g. "...so any specialty with no holders still becomes a row...").
findings.fix: Reword or reflow the comment at lines 83-85 so no single word is stranded on its own comment line.

findings.description: The vet names are separated by embedding a trailing space inside each name string: `vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + ' '`. This produces spurious trailing whitespace after the last (or only) vet in a specialty and couples the separator concern into the name value itself. Use Thymeleaf's iteration status (`iterStat.last`) to suppress the trailing space on the final element, or separate names with a comma, or let CSS handle the gap between inline spans.
findings.fix: Remove the trailing space from the `th:text` expression and instead conditionally append a separator only between elements, e.g. th:text="${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + (iterStat.last ? '' : ', ')}".

approved_aspects: Identity-equality risk (BaseEntity has no equals/hashCode) is correctly addressed by keying holdersBySpecialtyId on Specialty.getId() rather than on the Specialty object itself, and the comment explaining why is present
findSpecialties() Javadoc explicitly states why @Cacheable("vets") is omitted — a future reader will not wonder
LinkedHashMap preserves the name-order from findSpecialties() through to the model attribute, satisfying the stable-order acceptance criterion
Comparator.comparing(Vet::getLastName).thenComparing(Vet::getFirstName) produces a deterministic holder order within each specialty
@Query JPQL is correct for a Repository<Vet,Integer> querying a non-aggregate entity (Specialty) that Spring Data cannot derive automatically
